group_assessment.weighting: Two halves weighed apart. The corresponding laboratory cloned WWOX and is primary for the GENE, so the biochemistry of WW1/PPXY binding (co-IP, GST WW1 mutants) comes from native expertise and weighs as a strong observation. The proteomics was run on an established TAP-MS platform of a collaborating radiation-oncology laboratory (Chen J, one shared WWOX paper) and scored with that platform's MUSE model — an adjacent method, so the scoring and filtering are imported rather than designed for this bait. The pathway interpretation is the WWOX group's own and carries the investment of a laboratory that has argued a metabolic role for WWOX in prior work (refs 5, 10): that is a reason to weigh the INTERPRETATION of the enrichment below its observation. Neither group is primary for WWOX-related epileptic encephalopathy; nothing here is in neural cells.

entries.proposition: METHOD · SYSTEM: the whole interactome comes from one transformed human cell line, HEK293T, stably expressing a C-terminally SFB-tagged full-length WWOX. No neural cell, primary cell, tissue or endogenous-WWOX pull-down is used anywhere in the paper. DATO.
entries.snippet: HEK293T cells stably expressing SBP-S-FLAG (SFB) triple-tagged WWOX were generated as described previously (38).
entries.anchor: Materials and Methods › Vector Construct, Cell Culture, Transfection and Clone Selection for TAP-MS, sentence 1

entries.proposition: METHOD · EXPRESSION LEVEL: the claim that the chosen clones express tagged WWOX at a level similar to endogenous WWOX is asserted and not shown — no clone immunoblot appears in any figure (Figure 1 is a schematic) or supplement. The "physiological conditions" framing rests on this unshown comparison. DATO (absence of the panel).
entries.snippet: Twelve cell clones were isolated and examined for expression levels of tagged WWOX by immunoblotting and selected those with similar expression level as the endogenous WWOX protein to proceed with the TAP steps.
entries.anchor: Results › TAP-MS Based Proteomic Profiling of WWOX Interactome, sentence 3
entries.found_or_sought: sought — a clone blot was looked for in Figures 1-5 and Supplementary Files 1-4 and is not present

entries.proposition: METHOD · SPECIFICITY: non-specific binders are removed computationally (MUSE scoring, then the external CRAPome contaminant repository). No in-experiment negative-control purification (empty SFB vector or unrelated tagged bait in the same cells) is described in Methods, Results or the supplements. DATO (for what is described); the absence is a searched negative.
entries.snippet: To evaluate potential protein-protein interactions, assign probabilistic scores to individual interactions and eliminate non-specific interactions, the Minkowski distance-based unified probabilistic scoring environment (MUSE) statistical model was applied.
entries.anchor: Materials and Methods › Tandem Affinity Purification … MS Analysis, paragraph 2, sentence 2
entries.found_or_sought: sought — control TAP searched in Methods, Results, Figure 1 and Supplementary Files 1-2; none found

entries.proposition: METHOD · FILTER 1: 383 proteins present in both replicates were cut to 253 by CRAPome frequency < 0.2 — an external frequency across other laboratories' affinity purifications, not a control run in this experiment.
entries.snippet: From the identified 383 proteins, we narrowed down the list to 253 proteins with a CRAPome frequency < 0.2.
entries.anchor: Results › TAP-MS Based Proteomic Profiling, paragraph 2, sentence 3

entries.proposition: METHOD · FILTER 2 UNSTATED: the step from 253 to the final 216 "shortlisted based on the MUSE algorithm generated interaction scores" names no threshold. In Supplementary File 2 the lowest retained interaction score is 0.029 (recomputed from the xlsx container); the cutoff that excluded 37 proteins cannot be recovered from the paper. DATO (what is stated) + the unstated threshold as a declared limit.
entries.snippet: The data was further shortlisted based on the MUSE algorithm generated interaction scores (40) thus generating a final list of 216 WWOX prey proteins provided in Supplementary File 2.
entries.anchor: Results › TAP-MS Based Proteomic Profiling, paragraph 2, sentence 4
entries.found_or_sought: sought — threshold searched in Methods, Results, Figure 1 legend and Supplementary File 2 header; none stated

entries.proposition: DESIGN · REPLICATION: n = 2 purifications. Replicate yield differs (795 vs 594 proteins) and only 383 are shared; every downstream list is the intersection of two runs.
entries.snippet: We identified a total of 7,589 peptides from two replicates, corresponding to a total of 795 proteins in replicate-1 and 594 proteins in replicate-2 (Supplementary File 1).
entries.anchor: Results › TAP-MS Based Proteomic Profiling, paragraph 1, sentence 4

entries.proposition: FIGURE 1, inspected at native resolution (945x1324): a workflow schematic, not data. Its "Data Analysis" box prints "1389 interacting proteins" — the SUM of 795 + 594 — while its own Venn (412 | 383 | 211) gives 1,006 unique proteins as the text states; the box counts a protein found in both replicates twice. A labelling inconsistency, not a data error; it touches no downstream list.

entries.proposition: RESULT · TOP TIER: 14 prey with MUSE interaction score > 0.3 (a further 18 between 0.2 and 0.3). Confirmed against Supplementary File 2 by recount: 14 and 32. DATO.
entries.snippet: As per analysis with the MUSE algorithm (40), we identified 14 proteins with TAP-MS interaction scores (IS) > 0.3.
entries.anchor: Results › High Confidence WWOX Protein Interactors, sentence 1

entries.proposition: AUTHOR INTERPRETATION, not observation: "direct physical binding partner" is inferred from a probabilistic co-purification score. A TAP-MS score measures co-purification from lysate; it cannot distinguish direct binding from membership of a complex. INFERENZA (of the authors).
entries.snippet: These targets have a very high likelihood of being direct WWOX physical binding partners (Table 1 and Figure 2).
entries.anchor: Results › High Confidence WWOX Protein Interactors, sentence 2

entries.proposition: FIGURE 2, inspected at native resolution (980x1687): 32 bars (14 green > 0.3, 18 blue 0.2-0.3). Of every enzyme painted red in Figure 5B, exactly ONE appears among these 32 — BCKDHA, a blue bar near 0.21 with CRAPome frequency visibly raised. No PDH subunit, DLD, DLAT, HADHA/HADHB, ALDH, ACSL, ACADSB, MCCC2, HSD17B10 or PKM bar. The trafficking prey SEC23IP, VOPP1 and SCAMP3 are green bars. So the metabolic enzymes of the pathway story sit OUTSIDE the tier the authors themselves call high-confidence.

entries.proposition: METHOD · CO-IP: both partners are OVER-EXPRESSED by transient co-transfection (Myc-DDK-prey + GFP-WWOX) in HEK293T; no endogenous-protein co-IP is performed for any prey.
entries.snippet: For co-immunoprecipitation, HEK293T cells were co-transfected with either 1 μg of Myc-DDK-VOPP1, Myc-DDK-SCAMP3, or Myc-DDK-SEC23IP along with 1 μg of GFP-WWOX plasmid.
entries.anchor: Materials and Methods › Co-immunoprecipitation, sentence 4

entries.proposition: METHOD · CO-IP CONTROL: IgG is the only negative control. No single-transfection (Myc-prey alone, GFP alone) or unrelated-Myc-protein control is described, so GFP-tag or bead stickiness is not excluded beyond IgG.
entries.snippet: Corresponding IgG (MilliporeSigma, Burlington, MA, United States) was used as a negative control.
entries.anchor: Materials and Methods › Co-immunoprecipitation, sentence 8
entries.found_or_sought: sought — GFP-only / prey-only lanes searched in Methods and Figure 3A; none

entries.proposition: RESULT (text): reciprocal co-IP of WWOX with SEC23IP, SCAMP3 and VOPP1 — the three trafficking/endolysosomal prey are the only TAP-MS hits validated by a second method in this paper. DATO for co-association of the over-expressed proteins; "strong physical interaction" is the authors' wording.
entries.snippet: Indeed, co-IP of WWOX with SEC23IP, SCAMP3, and VOPP1 proteins demonstrated a strong physical interaction between WWOX and each of these proteins.
entries.anchor: Results › WWOX Physical Interaction With Members of Protein Complexes…, paragraph 1, sentence 6

entries.proposition: FIGURE 3A, inspected at native resolution (945x1200): six strips (anti-Myc left, anti-WWOX right) × lanes Input / IgG / Myc / GFP-WWOX; every IgG lane is blank and every Myc and GFP-WWOX IP lane carries a band, the VOPP1 anti-WWOX strip weakest. The panel agrees with the text. What it cannot show: no molecular-weight marker is printed in 3A, and the anti-WWOX antibody would detect endogenous WWOX as well as GFP-WWOX, so which WWOX species co-precipitates is not readable from the image; there is no single-transfection lane.
entries.snippet: Visual attestation of Figure 3A: IgG lanes blank in all six strips; bands in Myc and GFP-WWOX IP lanes for Myc-SEC23IP, Myc-SCAMP3, Myc-VOPP1 (anti-Myc) and in the matching anti-WWOX strips; no kDa ladder in panel A.
entries.anchor: Figure 3, panel A (PDF p. 7), native embedded JPEG 945x1200

entries.proposition: METHOD · GST PULL-DOWN: bacterially expressed GST-WW constructs are incubated with WHOLE-CELL LYSATE of HEK293T cells transfected with Myc-prey. This tests WW1 dependence of capture from a lysate; it does not test direct binding between purified proteins, because a bridging protein in the lysate is not excluded.
entries.snippet: GST pull-down assays were performed by addition of 10 μg of purified GST-fusion protein and 20 μl of Glutathione Sepharose 4B (50% slurry) to 600 μg of total cell lysate from HEK293T cells.
entries.anchor: Materials and Methods › GST Pull-Down Assay, sentence 6

experimental_context.system: GST fusion proteins from E. coli + HEK293T whole-cell lysate

entries.proposition: RESULT · WW1 DEPENDENCE (SEC23IP and SCAMP3 only): capture is lost with WW1 W44F/P47A and retained with the WW2 mutant. VOPP1 is not tested by pull-down in this paper; its WW1/PPPY dependence is cited from Bonin et al. DATO.
entries.snippet: Thus, the interaction with SEC23IP and SCAMP3 is lost when key functional residues of the WW1 domain are mutated, while the mutation in the WW2 domain (GST-Mut-WW2) does not affect the overall binding (Figure 3B).
entries.anchor: Results › WWOX Physical Interaction…, paragraph 2, sentence 3

experimental_context.system: GST fusion proteins from E. coli + HEK293T whole-cell lysate

entries.proposition: OVERCLAIM: "demonstrate … direct interacting partners" — neither the co-IP (over-expressed proteins, lysate) nor the pull-down (lysate) establishes directness. What is demonstrated is WW1-dependent co-association. The paper's own word "direct" should not be carried as a LEGEND observation.
entries.snippet: In summary, these results demonstrate that SEC23IP and SCAMP3 are indeed novel direct interacting partners of WWOX via WW1 domain.
entries.anchor: Results › WWOX Physical Interaction…, paragraph 2, sentence 4

experimental_context.system: GST fusion proteins from E. coli + HEK293T whole-cell lysate

The panel confirms the text's WW1-dependence; it carries no VOPP1 row.
entries.snippet: Visual attestation of Figure 3B: Myc-SEC23IP and Myc-SCAMP3 bands present with GST-WW1-2, GST-Mut-WW2, GST-WW1, GST-WWOX; absent with GST, GST-Mut-WW1, GST-WW2; Coomassie loading gel beneath; no VOPP1 row.

entries.proposition: EXTERNAL CORROBORATION CITED, not measured here: VOPP1–WWOX via WW1 and the 162PPPY165 motif rests on Bonin et al. 2018 (ref 46, PMID 30285739), which this corpus holds in the registry without a read receipt.
entries.snippet: Very recently, Bonin et al. (46) have also identified VOPP1 as a WWOX interactor in human cells by means of yeast-two hybrids and demonstrated that the WW1 region is the interacting domain mostly with the 162PPPY165 motif of VOPP1.
entries.anchor: Results › WWOX Physical Interaction…, paragraph 1, last sentence

entries.proposition: RESULT · MOTIF vs SCORE: prey with a PPX(Y/F)/LPX(Y/F) motif have a higher mean MUSE score (0.1875 vs 0.1287). Recomputed from Supplementary File 2 (67 vs 149 prey): means reproduce exactly; Student t = 3.36 (df 214) reproduces p ≈ 0.001; but Welch t = 2.64 and a Mann-Whitney z = 2.26 give p of roughly 0.009 and 0.02 — the difference survives, the reported strength depends on assuming equal variances in a visibly skewed distribution. DATO (reported) + reader recomputation.
entries.snippet: Proteins with-motifs displayed a significantly higher interaction score (mean interaction score = 0.1875, p < 0.001) as compared to proteins with no-motifs (mean interaction score = 0.1287, Figure 4C), thus suggesting as expected a higher affinity for direct physical WWOX binding.
entries.anchor: Results › WWOX WW1 Binding Motifs in TAP-MS Dataset, paragraph 2, last sentence

entries.proposition: METHOD · STATISTICS: the only hypothesis test performed by the authors is a two-tailed unpaired Student t-test on interaction scores; pathway statistics are imported from InnateDB. No test concerns metabolism as a measured quantity.
entries.snippet: The comparison of interaction scores between WWOX binding proteins with- and without-motif was done using statistical software GraphPad PRISM 7 and the Student's two-tailed unpaired t-test was used for comparisons.
entries.anchor: Materials and Methods › Statistical Methods, sentence 1

The legend speaks of comparing MEDIANS while the test named is a t-test on MEANS — a mismatch between caption and statistic.

entries.proposition: RESULT · NON-REPLICATION ACROSS METHODS: only 16 prey overlap with the GST-WW1 pull-down MS dataset of Abu-Odeh et al. (218 prey). The two WWOX interactomes largely disagree; the authors attribute it to method. DATO.

entries.proposition: TABLE 2: the 16 overlapping prey. Among them the metabolic enzymes HSD17B10 (0.13) and HADHA (0.06) — both with low scores here; no PDH subunit, DLD or ALDH is shared with the independent dataset.

entries.proposition: METHOD · ENRICHMENT: pathway p-values come from InnateDB. The paper states no background set (whole genome vs HEK293T-expressed or AP-MS-detectable proteome), no correction method in the text, and no control for the known over-representation of abundant mitochondrial/metabolic enzymes in affinity purifications. Supplementary File 4 lists a "corrected" p-value without naming the correction. Declared limit.

entries.proposition: RESULT · CONVERGENCE ON ACETYL-CoA IS A MAP READING, not a measurement: the statement that the enriched pathways "converge primarily in Acetyl-CoA generation" is a property of the KEGG pathway diagrams the prey were mapped onto. Any enrichment of BCAA, glycolytic, pyruvate and β-oxidation enzymes converges on acetyl-CoA by textbook topology. AUTHOR INTERPRETATION of annotation.
entries.snippet: Interestingly, all these highly significant pathways that derive from proteins, carbohydrates, and lipids breakdown converge primarily in Acetyl-CoA generation

Owner re-derivation before applying, 2026-09-14, ALDAZ-LOCATOR-REV-B-20260914: Data_Sheet_2.tsv rows 1-217 = bait + 216 prey then blank rows; Data_Sheet_4.tsv Val/Leu/Ile degradation, Glycolysis/Gluconeogenesis, Pyruvate metabolism and Fatty acid degradation give 18 distinct members, 17 by symbol in the 216 plus PKM2 = PKM (Entrez 5315); PDK3 and ALDH18A1 in the 216 and absent from File 4; DBT absent from the 216 (File 1 replicate sheets only); Figure 5B at native resolution: 17 distinct red names, HK2 and PFKL not drawn. Owner's check agreed with the auditor on every figure; amendment applied.

entries.proposition: DISCUSSION · PDC PRESENCE, with the scores the text omits: PDHA1, PDHB, DLAT and DLD are among the 216 — at interaction scores of 0.14, 0.19, 0.04 and 0.11 (Supplementary File 2, recomputed), i.e. ranks 89, 41, 203 and 114 of 216, none in Table 1. Presence in the prey list is DATO; their standing as WWOX interactors is low-confidence by the paper's own tiering.
entries.snippet: It is particularly intriguing that practically all members of the Pyruvate Dehydrogenase Complex (PDC), in charge of the enzymatic steps that catalyze the conversion of pyruvate (generated from glycolysis) into acetyl-CoA, can be found among the 216 proteins (Supplementary File 2)
entries.anchor: Discussion, paragraph 8, sentence 1

entries.proposition: AUTHOR INFERENCE from enrichment: WWOX "likely participates" in glycolysis and fatty acid degradation. The step from "prey enriched in pathway annotations" to "WWOX participates in the pathway" is not measured in this paper. INFERENZA (authors).
entries.snippet: Thus, suggesting that WWOX likely participates in glycolysis, fatty acid degradation and other pathways that converge primarily in Acetyl-CoA generation
entries.anchor: Discussion, paragraph 7, sentence 3

entries.proposition: AUTHORS' OWN CLOSING STRENGTH: the conclusion is phrased as "a significant lead" on partners with which WWOX "might interact" — weaker than the Results headings. This is the ceiling the source itself sets.
entries.snippet: In summary, our results provide a significant lead on subsets of protein partners and enzymatic complexes with which WWOX might interact with in order to carry out its metabolic functions and other significant biological roles.
entries.anchor: Discussion, last paragraph

entries.proposition: TRAFFICKING ROLE is a CANDIDACY, not a finding: from three validated co-associations plus an earlier SIMPLE interaction the authors conclude WWOX is "a prime candidate" for a role in ERES-to-Golgi and late-endosome-to-lysosome trafficking. No trafficking assay (cargo transport, ERES assembly, endosome morphology, lysosomal delivery) is performed. INFERENZA (authors).
entries.snippet: This in conjunction with the aforementioned observations involving SEC23IP, SCAMP3, and VOPP1 suggest that indeed WWOX is a prime candidate to play a relevant role in the homeostasis and regulation of perinuclear protein complexes related to protein trafficking between ERES to Golgi and from late endosomes to lysosomes.
entries.anchor: Discussion, paragraph 5
entries.found_or_sought: sought — any functional trafficking readout searched in Results and Figures 1-5; none

entries.proposition: SPECULATION labelled as such by the authors: WWOX–SEC23IP modulating COPII binding. IPOTESI (authors).
entries.snippet: Thus, it is possible to speculate that the WWOX-SEC23IP interaction might modulate binding of SEC23IP to the COPII complex and play an important role in ERES assembly or cargo transport.
entries.anchor: Discussion, paragraph 2, last sentence

entries.proposition: METABOLIC PHENOTYPE IS IMPORTED: the only metabolic measurements in the paper's argument are other laboratories' (Wwox KO MEFs: glucose uptake, glycolysis, respiration — refs 22, 56), cited in the Discussion. This paper measures no metabolic quantity.
entries.snippet: Abu-Remaileh and Aqeilan reported that Wwox KO mouse embryo fibroblasts displayed increase glucose uptake, enhanced glycolysis and reduced mitochondrial respiration
entries.anchor: Discussion, paragraph 10, sentence 1
entries.found_or_sought: sought — metabolite, respiration, flux or activity assay searched in Methods, Results, Figures, Supplementary Files; none

entries.proposition: NO COUPLING MECHANISM, stated by the authors themselves for the one metabolic mechanism they discuss.
entries.snippet: However, the exact mechanisms on how WWOX could affect HIF1α activity and in turn modulate cellular respiration are not clear.
entries.anchor: Discussion, paragraph 10, sentence 4

entries.proposition: FRAMING PREMISE: WWOX's own enzymatic substrate is unknown; the paper does not test the SDR activity or connect it to any prey.
entries.snippet: It is important to stress that WWOX is also an enzyme predicted to carry out NAD(H) or NADP(H)-dependent dehydrogenase reactions with yet to be identified substrate/s
entries.anchor: Introduction, paragraph 4

entries.proposition: MOTIF-LESS TOP PREY: 15 of the 32 top prey carry no WW-binding motif, which the authors read as binding elsewhere OR membership of larger complexes — i.e. the dataset itself cannot separate direct from indirect.
entries.snippet: On the other hand, among the list of top interactors with IS > 0.2, 15 of 32 proteins do not display canonical WW domain binding motifs suggesting that physical interactions may occur via other WWOX protein regions or some of these prey proteins could be members of larger protein complexes.
entries.anchor: Results › High Confidence WWOX Protein Interactors, last sentence

entries.proposition: "PHYSIOLOGICAL CONDITIONS" is the authors' framing of stable over-expression of a tagged construct in HEK293T; it licenses reading the whole prey list "in toto" as a portrait. The framing is not an experimental control. AUTHOR INTERPRETATION.
entries.snippet: We believe that since TAP-MS was performed under in-cellulo physiological conditions, much relevant information can be gained from analyzing the data in toto as a portrait for identifying protein networks, pathways and cellular compartments in which WWOX likely plays a functional role.
entries.anchor: Discussion, paragraph 7, sentence 1
